sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Tourcoing, on the Belgian border in the Lille metropolis, keeps its centre parking free but time-limited. The city runs a blue zone in which parking is free for one hour from arrival, from 9:00 to 12:00 and 14:00 to 19:00 Monday to Saturday except on public holidays, according to a page last modified on 19 March 2026 [0]. Residents of the zone can get a free resident card and professionals with premises in it a free professional card, on application to the town hall's roads department, with a vehicle registration document updated to the address in the zone [1]. The city says 137 spaces were recently added for a total of 2,321 surface and structure spaces in the centre, and that shops at Espace Saint-Christophe give 1h30 of free parking with a purchase, 4 hours for the cinema [2]. The city lists open-air blue-zone car parks at Grand'Place, Place de la Résistance, Rue Nationale, Place du Théâtre and the town hall [3]. The metropolis presents its low-emission zone as applying across all 95 communes from 1 January 2025, with a Crit'Air sticker required at all times and the ban targeting unclassified vehicles registered before 1 January 1997, with several exemptions and derogations; the page is undated, so its legal status in October 2026 is unverified [7]. We found no official page on paid on-street parking or a post-parking charge.

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The big project is a tramway for the Roubaix-Tourcoing area. The metropolis's Extramobile programme plans a new north-south line from Neuville-en-Ferrain through Tourcoing and Roubaix to Hem, an extension of tram line T from Tourcoing Centre to Gare de Tourcoing and an extension of line R to Wattrelos, 38 stations and 20.5 km for the whole project, with commissioning envisaged for 2033 for the north-south axis and 2035 for the east-west one. It is a plan, not built [12]. The same page says exchange hubs and park-and-ride areas will be created and estimates 60,000 trips a day at opening, without parking capacities [13]. The Boulevard Industriel green belt, with 3.6 km of planted boulevard and 11 km of cycle lanes at a cost of 20 million euros, lists maintained parking capacity for motorists among its advantages [14]. The page on the station district, written around 2020 to 2021, aims at a multimodal exchange hub and a park-and-ride to open in September 2021, which it does not confirm [11]. The home page announces an autumn funfair from 21 October to 1 November 2026, with a temporary car park on the Saint-Christophe forecourt [15]. The metropolis's Iléwatt on-street charging service has been rolling out since July 2024, with about 175 charging points in the 12 park-and-ride car parks and nearly 280 planned [6].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The metropolis lists Indigo as operator of the three centre car parks, Hôtel de Ville (rue de la Bienfaisance), Miss Cavell (avenue Allende) and Saint-Christophe (rue des Anges), among the 25 public car parks it lists in Lille, Roubaix and Tourcoing; the city's own page also links an Onepark car park [4][3]. In those car parks the charging prices for Indigo Neo, as of 1 July 2025, are 0.29 euro per kWh with a subscription, 0.45 occasional and 0.55 without an Indigo card [5]. The metropolis operates 12 park-and-ride sites with 5,500 spaces, reserved for ilévia or TER customers, where entry is free and exit needs a ticket validated the same day [8][9]. Metro line 2 and tram line T serve the city, with seven metro stations and four tram stops in Tourcoing [10].

Our data cover three car parks, from the metropolis's open data. Hôtel de Ville (434 spaces), over 26 days, averaged 92% on weekdays and 93% at weekends and reached full in single readings on Saturdays, so it is the most pressured car park in the centre. Miss Cavell (273) averaged 77% every day and stayed between about 73% and 81% in all readings. Saint-Christophe (757), measured for only 7 days, averaged 14% on weekdays and 10% at weekends, which is little use outside events.
